rendered: The review starts from the total global cobalt reserves, taken from the United States Geological Survey report on cobalt: 7 million metric tons[1]. It then applies a conservative yearly mining efficiency of ≈70%[2], and assumes that ≈40%[3] of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. Applying these reductions to the reserves, the cobalt usable for batteries comes to ≈2 million metric tons[4] globally. The introduction gives the same chain: the known reserves are recomputed with the same mining efficiency and battery share to give the usable battery-specific cobalt. ≈2 million[5]
